original_question: Let A be a self-adjoint cyclic operator on a Hilbert space, let φ be a cyclic vector for A, and let A_alpha = A + alpha(·, φ)φ be a rank-one perturbation with spectral measure mu_alpha taken with respect to φ. Characterize the singular continuous part of mu_alpha in terms of the unperturbed spectral measure mu.
target_in_paper: The unnumbered open problem in the discussion "Behavior of the Singular Continuous Spectrum," which asks for a characterization of the singular continuous part of the perturbed spectral measure in terms of the unperturbed operator/measure.
correct_elements: The draft already has the right core setup: a self-adjoint operator A, a cyclic vector φ, the rank-one perturbation A_alpha = A + alpha(·, φ)φ, the perturbed spectral measure mu_alpha taken with respect to φ, and the correct target of the question, namely the singular continuous part of the perturbed measure in relation to the unperturbed spectral measure mu.
missing_details: The paper’s setup is for a self-adjoint operator on a separable Hilbert space; in the general unbounded/form-bounded setting the perturbing vector is taken in H_{-1}(A), not just arbitrarily in H.
The perturbation parameter should be quantified explicitly as alpha in R, typically for the whole family of rank-one perturbations.
mu and mu_alpha should be identified as the scalar spectral measures of A and A_alpha with respect to the same vector φ.
The phrase "self-adjoint cyclic operator" should be replaced by "self-adjoint operator with cyclic vector φ"; cyclicity belongs to the vector, not to the operator as stated in the draft.
The paper frames this as an open characterization problem, not as a theorem already proved in the paper.
Nearby context in the paper gives only one-sided sufficient conditions for absence of singular continuous spectrum on a closed interval; that should not be confused with a full characterization.
If one wants a local version, the interval I should be specified as a closed interval, and the question should ask for the vanishing or structure of (mu_alpha)_{sc} on I.
refined_question: Let A be a self-adjoint operator on a separable Hilbert space H, and let φ be a cyclic vector for A (more generally, in the paper’s rank-one perturbation setup, φ is allowed in H_{-1}(A) so that the perturbations are well defined). For each real alpha, define the rank-one perturbation A_alpha = A + alpha(·, φ)φ, and let mu and mu_alpha denote the scalar spectral measures of A and A_alpha with respect to φ. Characterize, in terms of the unperturbed spectral measure mu, the singular continuous part (mu_alpha)_{sc} of mu_alpha.
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s actual intent. The nearest official formulation is not a numbered conjecture or theorem but an explicit open problem: the paper states that a characterization of the singular continuous part of the perturbed operator’s spectral measure in terms of the unperturbed operator remains open. The surrounding discussion fixes the standard rank-one perturbation family A_alpha = A + alpha(·, φ)φ and the associated scalar spectral measures with respect to the cyclic vector φ. The nearby result is only a sufficient criterion for pure absolute continuity on a closed interval, so the refined question should stay as a sharp open characterization problem and should not be broadened into a more general question about all singular spectrum or all spectral types.
